rationale: The candidate reads as a compact but overworked mass with a noisy stepped/blended silhouette rather than one dominant, legible building idea. Across the four views it is only partly coherent; the top and oblique views suggest a flattened, twisted block, while the front/opposite views reveal a bulky object with many clipped protrusions and no clear sectional order. The parcel is technically contained, but the mass does not convincingly organize itself to the green boundary or to the verified access edge. The blue frontage edge is answered by a sealed or semantically weak ground condition rather than a public threshold, court, seam, or entry void. For the program, a neighborhood_living brief needs an active ground relation and a usable public void/terrace; here the visible void is minimal and decorative, and the section does not establish a believable inhabitated terrace or clear mixed-use ground support. The form also appears close to a fragmented book-aggregation artifact, which undermines hierarchy and continuity. The main useful precedent principle is not the literal massing, but the idea of a courtyard/threshold and grounded public edge. A better next move would be to preserve the compact dominant anchor, clean the silhouette, and carve a legible access-side void or terrace rather than further stacking pieces.
